title: Lift a specified continuous block factorization along an open immersion
statement: Let E be a normed field, g:W to V an open immersion, R a ring sheaf identified by an invertible monoid morphism e with continuous E coefficients, and f:R^m to R^n. Suppose a specified factorization of its matrix after composition with g is P times a reindexed identity-and-zero block times Q, where P and Q have unit determinants and the selected row and column maps Fin r into Fin n and Fin m are injective. Then the pulled-back source and target split as R_W^r plus finite-free complements, and pulled-back f is diag(identity,zero) under these isomorphisms. No locally constant-rank, noetherian or covering hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: For continuous-function coefficients, identify each regular-module endomorphism with its global value at one. Linearity gives multiplication by that function on every section; naturality identifies local values with its restriction. Multiplication by a global continuous function gives the inverse assignment. Check addition and composition sectionwise.

Biproduct inclusions and projections identify finite-free maps with matrices compatibly with composition. Thus P and Q and their inverse matrices give module automorphisms. The chosen injections identify the selected entries with Fin r and their complements with finite sets.

Use the monoidal inverse-image/localization-restriction comparison along the open immersion. It identifies the pulled-back coefficient sheaf with continuous functions on W, and the given matrix entries with composition along g. Transport by e and the finite-biproduct comparisons. The explicit factorization now gives the equality of module maps. Enumerate the complementary finite sets by Fin of their cardinalities.

proof_origin.place: C1 completed the three-step Lean proof: continuous-coefficient regular-module endomorphisms, finite-biproduct matrices and block splitting, then monoidal localization restriction and pullback assembly. The repair reuses the existing private CategoryTheory.pushforwardRingMonObj from Sheaf.AlgebraicGeometry.CondensedFieldContinuousRealization through a proof-only import all, deleting its duplicate. The coefficient and matrix argument follows the proved p-adic analogue WeilConjectures.SixFunctors.ProEtale.Adic.UnitMatrix, adapted to continuous coefficients and the finite-coefficient inverse-image API.
